newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end firm after Left election win. [CORRECTED 17:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: French stocks end firm after Left election win. [CORRECTED 17:27 GMT]

text.p: French shares ended higher on Monday, defying widespread expectations of a drastic fall after Sunday's Socialist election victory and the need for Communist support, traders said.

One senior broker said the market recovery was "amazing" and the volume was huge. But much of the business was short-covering on trading positions rather than buying by fund managers, she said. "I can't believe its institutional," she said.

The CAC-40 index closed up 17.71 points or 0.68 percent at 2,601.45. The CAC-40 futures contract was up four at 2,571 from Friday's close. Volume was a heavy 15.76 billion francs. (Corrects level of volume from 12.76 to 15.76 billion francs)
Volume was among the heaviest in recent sessions and follows Friday's trading above 18 billion francs, swollen by the expiry of May futures and options contracts.
The CAC index hit a session high of 2,645.86, running up gains of more than two percent in the afternoon before retreating as operators thought the climb was overdone.

Share prices drew support from firm bonds and the franc, and a fairly benign view of the Socialists. The senior broker cited a New York Times article which may have mitigated the impact of the strong position of the French Communists.

"The market is reassured for the time being," equities strategist Michelle Jardin at Credit Lyonnais Securities said. "The Socialists have won, if not an absolute majority, at least a big success. Investors are not worried about the weight of the Communists and therefore the path towards the euro."
Merrill Lynch strategist Brian Allworthy said stocks to pick were those which were "masters of their destiny, capital rather than labour intensive and open to international (markets)".
Consumer and retail stocks led the gains, on hopes of a Socialist-led boost to purchasing power, while defence and privatisation shares took heavy hits.
Among big risers were drinks group Pernod Ricard, rising 8.89 percent to 300 francs, LVMH gains 1.43 percent to 1,418, L'Oreal adds 3.48 percent to 2,168.
Carrefour, a blue chip favoured among international investors, rose 3.91 percent to 3,938, Bic added 3.53 percent to 880, while Eridania Beghin-Say jumped 2.85 percent to 831.
Danone advanced 1.73 percent to 884, Promodes rose 1.79 percent to 1,990.
Elf Aquitaine surged 3.99 percent to 600, helped by Friday's first-half profit forecast.
